mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns over the horizon are not statistically lower than during pre-trend periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by declining unemployment (UNRATE) creates a dual labor market signal that predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases over the same month
failure_condition: The interaction term (PAYEMS * -UNRATE) shows a p-value > 0.1 in a 20-day ahead regression with robust standard errors.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in consumer demand proxies (HOUST) coinciding with a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a shift toward services-driven growth, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by at least 10% while INDPRO decreases over the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from the mean of the prior 30-day window (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 105 for three consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness that is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO remains below 105 for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p-value > 0.1) during the contraction period.

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in CPIAUCSL exceeds +2% while FEDFUNDS remains below 4%, it indicates aggressive monetary easing that tends to boost equity valuations, producing positive 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not higher than the 30-day average preceding the signal (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in job openings (PAYEMS) exceeding 200,000 in a month without a corresponding rise in layoffs, suggests labor market loosening that precedes positive S&P 500 returns within 5 days.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are flat or negative despite the signal (p-value < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining retail sales (not available in the provided proxies - skip this) - instead: A prolonged decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 108 suggests structural supply constraints that predict negative 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not negative in at least 70% of instances of INDPRO decline (frequency test).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls below 4%, it creates expectations of future rate cuts that lower real discount rates, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the 3-month pre-signal average (p-value > 0.1).
